data.name: result
data.source: app.readApprovalQueue.execute — one list_entry_decisions read per agent, because BattleGrid publishes no account-wide decision read

data.name: authority
data.source: app.readAnswerAuthority.execute — the same HeldScopes the write guard reads

data.name: problem
data.source: searchParams — the reason a refused answer redirected back with

data.name: note
data.source: searchParams — a cancel that succeeded, said rather than silently redirected

components.purpose: Show every trade an agent proposed and is waiting on a human for, across every agent, with how long each has left before it expires.
components.current_implementation: max-w-3xl centred column, space-y-4, p-6 — the queue skeleton /pending already wears. h1 'Trades waiting for your answer', `<CarriedProblem>`, an optional role=status note, the fifteen-minute explainer, an optional step-up link when authority is absent, then `<ApprovalQueue>`.
constraints: No currency amount may appear (PE-2). BattleGrid computes no position size until a decision is accepted, so any figure here would be this product's arithmetic wearing the platform's authority, about money. tests/agent/approval-queue.test.ts scans this file for currency formatting and for the money-shaped budget fields.
'Nothing is waiting' and 'the queue could not be read' must never render as the same state — the requirement's own scenario, and on this surface the difference is a real trade expiring unanswered.
The step-up link must stay reachable from here and not only from a decision page: tests/architecture/reachability.test.ts requires a route to be offered from somewhere that is not itself a mutation.

The page renders whole from one server round trip; the only client code is the shared nav and PerformButton further in. Client-side polling or auto-refresh would change behavior and is requires-spec-change — the operator explicitly asked for no polling watch.

components.purpose: The waiting decisions themselves, grouped under the agent that proposed each one.
components.current_implementation: `<ApprovalQueue>` (approval-queue.tsx). Each group is a section headed by a link to its agent; each decision is a bordered consequence card carrying entry/stop/target/conviction as a `<dl>`, the proportion sentence, the model's reasoning, and one link to the answer page. Unreachable agents render above everything in a role=alert danger block with `<WhyNotLoaded>` per agent.
constraints: The agent is named at the group, never on the decision view. `PendingDecisionView` is asserted to carry exactly `decision` and `msRemaining` so there is nowhere on it for an amount to appear; grouping keeps that guard exactly as strong while still naming who proposed what.
The empty heading stays qualified whenever any agent went unread — 'Nothing is waiting from the agents that answered'. The unqualified claim is the lie this component exists to refuse.
No control is offered on a list row. The consequence has to be stated before cancel is reachable, and a control on a row is a control without one.

components.purpose: How long is left to answer, in units somebody under time pressure can act on.
components.current_implementation: Rendered from `msRemaining`, derived server-side and floored at zero. Null renders 'No expiry was sent for this decision'; zero renders 'The window has closed — this can no longer be answered'.
constraints: Must not be rebuilt from `expiresAt` in the component. The Iron Rule permits the server-side derivation and forbids the client one, and it is also what stops this figure disagreeing with the liveness the binding checks.
A missing expiry is unknown, never 'expires now'. Guessing in either direction is a claim about someone else's money that nobody made.

This is the most perishable thing on the page and stays beside each decision rather than once at the top. It is rendered at request time and does not tick — a design implying a live countdown would be claiming behavior the page does not have.

components.purpose: Name the agents that could not be asked, so a partial read is never read as an empty account.
components.current_implementation: role=alert danger block listing each agent with the platform's own reason and `<WhyNotLoaded>` beneath it. Rendered above the groups on the waiting branch and above the empty heading on the none branch.
constraints: role=alert must survive.
Must keep rendering on the 'none' branch — that is exactly the case where its absence would be most misleading, because the page otherwise reads as an account with nothing waiting.

components.purpose: Offer fund-committing authority from a page that mutates nothing, for an operator who wants it before a decision arrives.
components.current_implementation: A plain underlined link in a text-sm secondary paragraph, rendered only when authority is absent, saying the queue below is readable without it.
constraints: Absent entirely when the authority is held — not a disabled control and not an 'already granted' variant.
Must not be styled as a call to action. The product's standing posture is that most users never need this, and a prominent ask here would undercut the claim the connect page makes.

components.purpose: Show the refusal that bounced a submitted cancel back here.
components.current_implementation: Shared `CarriedProblem` (carried-problem.tsx) — DT-0004 danger treatment, role=alert, semibold 'Refused: ' prefix. Renders null without a problem, which is what makes the unconditional mount free.
constraints: role=alert must survive.
Shared by twelve surfaces now — restyle in the component, never per page.
The reason is domain- or platform-authored and unbounded: wrap rather than clip, and never truncate or paraphrase.
Rendering nothing when there is no problem is load-bearing — no reserved empty slot, no placeholder.

components.purpose: Say that a cancel succeeded, rather than redirecting silently.
components.current_implementation: role=status notice block — notice tokens, never danger — carrying the sentence the action set ('The proposal was cancelled. Nothing was bought or sold.').
constraints: Notice never borrows danger's colour (system.json principle): a successful cancel is not a failure.
Must not be removed as noise. A silent redirect is how an account moves without its operator learning it did, and this surface answers a money question.

components.purpose: Say whether a failed read was a refusal or an outage, because the two have different next steps.
components.current_implementation: Shared `WhyNotLoaded`, taking the `FailureCause` carried through from the port on both the roster failure and each per-agent failure.
constraints: The refused/unreachable distinction is spec-bearing — telling somebody with a bad credential to wait out an outage that is not happening is the mistake this component exists to stop.

flows.name: Read what is waiting
steps: read each agent's proposals with levels, conviction and reasoning
see how long each has left
follow one into its answer page

flows.name: Some agents could not be asked
steps: the danger block names the agents that failed and why
the groups below are explicitly not the whole account

flows.name: Nothing is waiting
steps: read that no agent has a trade waiting — qualified when any agent went unread

flows.name: A cancel lands back here
steps: cancel a proposal from its decision page
return with a status note saying nothing was bought or sold
the cancelled decision is no longer listed

accessibility.notes: The problem banner and the unreachable-agents block both carry role=alert and can be on screen together; the success note carries role=status. Focus ring is global (focus-visible, 2px). Every state change is a full navigation.
